title: Term
description: The class of glossary term records. A term is an INSTANCE — a definition entry seated in a glossary (content/glossary/terms/) — never a schema. What a kind of record must look like is a CLASS, and classes seat in the schema pool (lib/schemas/); a term that needs one points at it with specified-by rather than trying to be it.
$comment: This class replaces the doctrine under which 'a term IS a JSON Schema' and the glossary doubled as the schema pool. That identity is exactly the class/instance conflation the firm keeps re-deriving its way back into: a record that is simultaneously the contract and a thing under contract cannot be spoken about intelligibly, because every sentence about it is true at one level and false at the other. So: classes in lib, instances in content, and a term is an instance. Its definition is prose a reader uses; the machine-checkable shape of the things the term names, when there is one, lives in the class the term points at.

id.$comment: Equal to the record's basename; the glossary resolves a term by the name it is filed under.

name.$comment: What the term is called, as it is said.

definition.$comment: What the term means, as prose a reader uses. One term, one place it is defined — the content-librarian's rule.

specified-by.$comment: The class in the schema pool that gives the things this term names their machine-checkable shape, when there is one. The term defines the word; the class constrains the records.

x-evidence.description: In-corpus citations (file/line + short quote) grounding the term's evidence grade; optional.
